summary: A feature article on a growing movement of seniors embracing active lifestyles, told through profiles of joggers, swimmers and cyclists. It covers community initiatives, the FitSeniors app, mental health benefits, and the Steps to Strength program, concluding that it is never too late to start living actively.
one_line: Profiles of seniors who run, swim and cycle, plus community programs, tech and mental health benefits supporting active ageing.
key_facts: Michael Thomson is a 72-year-old former accountant who began early morning jogging after retirement and started the routine in September of the previous year.
Lillian Davis, 78, swims laps at the local indoor pool, having started in the fall of 2023, and says she feared arthritis would end her active days.
Sarah Jennings, a community health organizer, designed senior programs ranging from guided morning walks to chair yoga classes.
Senior-focused initiatives have sprouted since September 2023, engaging thousands of local seniors.
Personal trainer Jordan Martin launched the 'FitSeniors' app in November 2023, letting users track activity, set health goals and join virtual challenges.
Dr. Emily Stanton, a geriatric psychologist, says physical activity and mental health form a virtuous cycle.
Reported benefits of active lifestyles include reduced depression, sharpened cognitive functions and new friendships.
'Steps to Strength' offers low-impact exercises, nutrition education, routine check-ups and motivational workshops, led by facilitator Karen Lewis.
'Steps to Strength' began rolling out in neighborhoods in December 2023.
Judy and Bill Harrison, a couple in their eighties, became cycling advocates after a community cycling event in January 2024.
The author met Michael Thomson on a crisp October morning in 2023.
